timed_text.text: Day 17.
Before we go any deeper into competition performance, I need to ask you something.
Why are you doing this?
Not the athletic goals, not the starting spot or the stats or the scholarship.
I mean the bigger picture.
What are the things in your life that matter most?
The people, the relationships, the responsibilities that your athletic career supposed
to serve?
Bill Bessick calls this, keeping the first things first.
And what he found working with professional athletes at the highest level is that the
ones who burn out or lose motivation or who hit performance plateaus that can't climb
out of, they've usually lost their connection to their why.
When sport becomes the only thing, it becomes the wrong thing.
Because sport is not the point.
Sport is just the vehicle.
The relationships you build through it, the character develops, the future it creates,
that's the point.
Family, friends, health, academics, the people counting on you.
The version of yourself, you're building beyond the field.
When you stay connected to that, when you compete for something bigger than the scoreboard,
you're tougher to break because the foundation is bigger than any outcome.
On your screen, you're going to name your first things.
The ones that matter most regardless of whether you have ever, the ones that matter most
regardless of whether you ever play another game.

cards.prompt: Family — Who are the people in your family that your athletic journey is connected to? Why does competing well matter when you think about them?
Friends and teammates — Who in your life shows up for you regardless of performance? Why do those relationships matter to how you compete?
Health — Your body is the vehicle. What does taking care of it mean to you beyond sport — for the life you're building after the final game?
Academics and future — What are you building outside the lines? Why does the person you're becoming in the classroom and in the real world matter?
Now — write one sentence: 'I compete because...' Let it be honest. Let it be bigger than wins and losses.

timed_text.text: That why is now saved in your profile? Read it when competition stops feeling worth it. Read it when the
training is hard and the results aren't showing up yet. The athletes who last, who keep competing at a high
level when everything gets difficult, they've never lost their connection to that answer. After you
finish, day 17 is complete.
